strengths: 5th-largest district economy in Karnataka - GDDP Rs 99,527 crore (2024-25), 3.4% of state GSDP, and one of its most services-heavy districts (services 67.3%, 3rd-highest share in the state, 2024-25)
Karnataka's 2nd-largest software exporter and the anchor of the KDEM 'Beyond Bengaluru' Mysuru cluster (Tier-2 hub for IT/ITeS, ESDM, cybersecurity, GCCs and startups)
Home to Infosys' 337-acre Mysuru campus and Global Education Centre - described as the world's largest corporate training centre (~14,000 trainees at a time)
India's heritage-tourism capital - Mysuru Palace drew ~40.6 lakh visitors in 2023-24 (incl. ~34,600 foreign tourists), the highest in a decade, anchored by the Dasara festival

Diversified manufacturing base - BEML, JK/Vikrant Tyres, L&T, Automotive Axles, Rane and Kirloskar across eight KIADB industrial areas and two Special Investment Regions (Hebbal ~3,799 acres, Thandya ~3,198 acres)

Water-secure by Karnataka standards - all nine taluks now in the Safe groundwater category (Mysuru taluk, Semi-Critical under GEC 2020, recovered to 62.49% Safe by GEC 2024), with irrigation ~71% canal-fed from the Cauvery and Kabini
Deep knowledge base - University of Mysuru, CSIR-CFTRI, JSS and NIE, with ~40,000 engineering and degree students in the cluster (KDEM)
GI-tagged heritage industries - Mysore Silk (KSIC), Mysore Sandalwood lineage, and Nanjangud Rasabale banana
challenges: Per-capita income only Rs 2.69 lakh (2024-25) - about 70% of the state average of Rs 3.86 lakh, ranking 17th of 31 districts despite the large aggregate economy

Credit is urban-concentrated - the CD ratio is a healthy 81.63% (31.03.2025, above the state's 77.25%), but about 73% of advances sit in Mysuru city, leaving rural taluks (Hunsur, H.D. Kote, Periyapatna) under-served
IT growth beyond the Infosys anchor is still early - the wider GCC, startup and ESDM base needs depth to reach the KDEM 2030 targets
Sharp rural-urban divide - rural literacy ~63.3% against urban ~86.1%, and ~54% of workers are still in agriculture
Tourism is seasonal and Dasara-concentrated, with visitor pressure on heritage assets and limited high-value/overnight tourism spread
Agriculture is exposed to Cauvery-basin water-sharing cycles and to FCV-tobacco demand and regulatory pressure in Hunsur/Periyapatna
Post-harvest storage gap - about 9 lakh MT capacity against an estimated 15 lakh MT requirement (NABARD PLP)
Industrial data is dated - the last District Industrial Profile (DIC/MSME) is from 2010-11; current MSME, employment and turnover figures need a fresh survey
opportunities: Convert the KDEM 'Beyond Bengaluru' push into a genuine second tech city - GCC and ESDM parks targeting a USD 10 billion digital economy and ~1.5 lakh digital jobs by 2030
Lift per-capita income toward the state average by deepening high-value services (IT, GCCs, tourism) and modern manufacturing on the existing base

Deepen rural and MSME/manufacturing credit - the district's healthy CD ratio (81.63%) is concentrated in the city, so extending agri-value-chain and enterprise lending into the rural taluks is the opportunity
Grow high-value, year-round and heritage/eco/wellness tourism circuits (Palace, Chamundi Hills, Nagarhole, Kabini, Srirangapatna) beyond the Dasara peak
Expand agro-processing and FPO-led value chains and close the storage gap - CFTRI-backed food processing, Nanjangud banana, sericulture and dairy
Leverage water security and the Cauvery-Kabini canal network to modernise irrigation and diversify cropping while other Karnataka districts face groundwater stress
Build ESDM / electronics manufacturing in the Thandya and upcoming Kochanahalli industrial areas, adjacent to the IT and skilling ecosystem

summary.note: Mysuru taluk - the only block classed Semi-Critical under the NABARD PLP (GEC 2020) - has recovered to Safe in the latest CGWB assessments (INGRES): stage of extraction 65.86% (GEC 2023) and 62.49% (GEC 2024), both within the Safe band (<=70%). The other eight taluks were already Safe, so all nine are now Safe. District stage of extraction was ~51% under GEC 2020 (net draft 37,493 Ham of 73,122 Ham recharge) and the District Ground Water Office / CGWB report the district firmly Safe (~55%) as of 2023-24, with the water table averaging ~26.4 ft and rising ~0.32 m over 2015-2024 - versus Bengaluru's over-100% extraction, and against a Karnataka picture of 44 over-exploited taluks statewide.

groundwater.roadmapImplication: Unlike North Karnataka, groundwater is not the binding constraint here. The priority is efficient use of the Cauvery-Kabini canal command, recharge and lake rejuvenation (especially around Mysuru taluk), not extraction control.

dc.headline: Mysuru is Karnataka's 5th-largest district economy (GDDP Rs 99,527 cr) and its 2nd-largest software exporter, yet per-capita income (Rs 2.69L) is only ~70% of the state average (rank 17/31). The agenda is converting a strong services-and-heritage base into higher incomes, and extending its healthy but city-concentrated bank credit into the rural taluks.

kdem.headline: Mysuru is KDEM's flagship 'Beyond Bengaluru' cluster - Karnataka's 2nd-largest software exporter, anchored by Infosys' Global Education Centre. The USD 10 bn / ~1.5 lakh-jobs 2030 vision needs a broader GCC, startup and ESDM base; 240+ startups and 10,000 plug-and-play seats (4,000 occupied) are the current base.

industrial.headline: Mysuru has a manufacturing base most districts lack - BEML, JK/Vikrant Tyres, L&T, Automotive Axles, Rane and Kirloskar across eight KIADB areas and two Special Investment Regions (~7,000 acres). The agenda is modernisation toward ESDM/EV and converting the base into higher incomes and credit.

revenue.headline: Revenue and land are central to the industrial and IT build-out: the Hebbal and Thandya Special Investment Regions (~7,000 acres) and the upcoming Kochanahalli area need clean land records and timely acquisition. Mysuru is largely water-secure, easing the usual land-water conflicts.

agriculture.headline: Canal-fed and water-secure - ~71% of net irrigated area is Cauvery-Kabini canal command and all 9 taluks are groundwater-Safe (Mysuru taluk recovered from Semi-Critical). Paddy, ragi, sugarcane and FCV tobacco (Hunsur/Periyapatna) run alongside an under-built agro-processing and FPO base and a post-harvest storage gap.

water.headline: Water is a strength, not a crisis: district groundwater extraction is ~51-55% (Safe), all 9 taluks Safe (Mysuru taluk recovered from Semi-Critical to 62.49% in GEC 2024), and irrigation is ~71% canal-fed from the Cauvery and Kabini. The task is efficiency, recharge and lake rejuvenation, not extraction control.

health.headline: Mysuru city is a tertiary-care hub (Mysore Medical College / K.R. Hospital, JSS, Apollo BGS, Columbia Asia, Narayana; ~3,500+ beds), but sub-centres (354 vs ~600 norm) and CHCs (9 vs ~25 norm) fall short in rural taluks. Facility counts need a fresh audit (CHC count is 2010-11).

education.headline: Literacy is 72.8% with a sharp rural-urban gap (63.3% vs 86.1%). Mysuru's strength is its knowledge base - University of Mysuru, NIE, KSOU, JSS and CFTRI, with ~40,000 engineering and degree students in the cluster - which can feed the KDEM cluster if skilling aligns to IT/ESDM and GCC demand.

minister.headline: Mysuru: 30 lakh people, Karnataka's 5th-largest district economy (GDDP Rs 99,527 cr) and its heritage-and-tech capital - but per-capita income is only Rs 2.69L (~70% of state, rank 17/31), even though bank credit is healthy (CD ratio 82%). Indicative Rs 16,000 Cr scaffold across 3 phases to build the second knowledge city.
